candidate.title: Directed conditional residual transport with codeword separation
candidate.equation: For each valid row i, let a_i = argmin_c ||source_i-codebook_c||_2^2, let r_i = target_i-source_i, and let u_i = codebook_{a_i}-source_i. Define v_i = r_i-u_i and s_i = ||v_i||_2^2. Let w_ic = softmax_c(-||source_i-codebook_c||_2^2/tau)_c and p_c = sum_i mask_i w_ic / sum_i mask_i. Let d_i = min_{c: c != a_i} ||codebook_{a_i}-codebook_c||_2. L = lambda * [sum_i mask_i * (s_i + separation * relu(margin-d_i)^2) / sum_i mask_i + balance * sum_c(p_c-1/C)^2].

symbols.codebook_c: Codeword c in the supplied codebook.
symbols.a_i: Nearest codeword index to source_i under squared Euclidean distance.
symbols.r_i: Observed directed behavior residual from source_i to target_i.
symbols.u_i: Source-side codebook residual from source_i to its selected codeword.
symbols.v_i: Mismatch between the observed behavior residual and the source-side codebook residual.
symbols.s_i: Squared norm of the residual mismatch v_i.
symbols.d_i: Distance from the selected source codeword to its nearest other codeword.
symbols.w_ic: Soft source assignment probability for row i and codeword c.
symbols.p_c: Mask-weighted average soft usage probability of codeword c.
symbols.margin: Minimum desired distance from a selected codeword to its nearest alternative.
symbols.separation: Weight of the codeword-separation term relative to residual transport.
symbols.balance: Strength of the source-usage balancing term.

candidate.behaviour_signal: The directed residual target_i - source_i, conditioned on the source's selected codeword and soft source-side usage.
candidate.codebook_interaction: The residual mismatch term moves the selected source codeword to model the source-conditioned behavior residual; it does not regress both endpoints toward a common codeword. The separation hinge repels a selected codeword from its nearest alternative when their distance is below margin, and the usage term opposes concentrated source-side assignments. The nearest-codeword selection and nearest-other selection are discrete; gradients act on the selected codeword vectors and the soft usage probabilities.
candidate.encoder_interaction: Both source and target have nonzero gradients through the residual mismatch, and source also has a nonzero gradient through soft usage. The host discards encoder gradients, so exported-code changes depend on the codebook gradient.
candidate.risk: The residual target may encode behavior directions poorly aligned with the recommender's ranking objective, and codebook residual fitting can perturb assignments without improving held-out retrieval. The separation and balance penalties may conflict with residual fit, distort useful code geometry, or fail to preserve L1-to-L2 branching despite maintaining level-0 usage.
candidate.falsifier: Reject if held-out pair-level ER does not rise or if level-0 Gini exceeds 0.216, L1-to-L2 branches fall below 65.91, train-to-test frequency drift grows, or sequence information falls. A smaller median nearest-neighbor codeword distance or lower endpoint separation than control falsifies the intended anti-convergence safeguard.
candidate.why_not_the_measured_failures: Unlike inert encoder-only losses, the residual mismatch and separation terms deliver nonzero codebook gradients. Unlike the collapsed pairwise assignment cross-entropy, this objective conditions transport on the directed source residual and does not pull the pair's two endpoint codewords together; it additionally repels nearby codewords and penalizes imbalanced source usage. It remains subject to the frozen downstream and structure checks.
